limitations: No filesystem atomicity claim beyond the supplied-callback mutation window
This scan does not claim shipped runtime exposure or full repository security coverage
scope.runtimeStatus: No new runtime test was required for a candidate because discovery found none; prior focused controls remain the bounded implementation evidence.
scope.summary: Bounded security review of the exact 21.x 17-file source-admission patch.
scope.validationMode: Static compact-diff discovery plus existing focused callback and physical-source negative controls

assets: Integrity of source-bound Sass inventory, argument, seal, regression, and RC verification results
Correct attribution of current versus historical source bytes
Integrity and availability of local verification runs and CI gate decisions
assumptions: The local filesystem and repository checkout are trusted except for mutation performed through the supplied callback during one invocation
Ordinary concurrent external filesystem mutation outside the callback model is not claimed to be made atomic
This scan is limited to the exact 17-file 21.x working-tree patch and directly supporting call sites
attackerCapabilities: A caller can supply a read callback and metadata objects to exported helper APIs
A callback can return crafted bytes, mutate files during a verification call, or expose hostile object methods
Repository-controlled configuration and paths may be malformed or unexpectedly large
securityObjectives: Do not admit a current-source claim unless every bound physical file still matches its manifest identity after callback-bearing work
Reject known owned paths with foreign hashes and preserve non-owned passthrough semantics without relabeling
Do not execute attacker-controlled commands or escape the intended repository paths
Bound callback/object behavior so hostile inputs cannot bypass comparisons or create disproportionate resource use
Keep tests and production adapters aligned on the same security property
threatModel.summary: The patch changes build/audit admission code that decides whether generated Sass API reports may claim the current workspace source. The security-sensitive boundary is between caller-supplied read callbacks and metadata, and trusted physical files and their bound hashes.
trustBoundaries: Caller-supplied read callback versus direct physical filesystem reads
Caller-supplied metadata/hash claims versus manifest-bound source identities
Historical reference material versus the current workspace source claim
Path/configuration input versus repository-root containment and command execution
